message.content:
I need to understand the "data layer" of this repository and identify persistent entity types defined there. 

1. First, explore the top-level directory structure to understand the repo layout.
2. Look for a "data" layer — this could be a package named "data", "database", "db", "entities", "models", "persistence", or similar.
3. Once found, list all persistent entity types (classes, interfaces, types) defined in that layer — things like User, Organization, Project, etc.
4. Report: the path to the data layer, and a complete list of all entity type names defined there with their file paths.

Be very thorough — check multiple naming conventions. This appears to be a monorepo so check inside packages/, libs/, modules/, src/, apps/, etc.

attachment.content:
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

106		s.userCreateMu.Lock()
107		defer s.userCreateMu.Unlock()
108	
109		limitOne := 1
110		users, err := s.driver.ListUsers(ctx, &FindUser{Limit: &limitOne})
111		if err != nil {
112			return nil, false, err
113		}
114		if len(users) > 0 {

116		}

151				user, ok := cache.(*User)
152				if ok {
153					return user, nil
154				}
155			}
156		}
157	
158		list, err := s.ListUsers(ctx, find)
159		if err != nil {
160			return nil, err
161		}
162		if len(list) == 0 {
163			return nil, nil
164		}
165	
166		user := list[0]
167		s.userCache.Set(ctx, userCacheKey(user.ID), user)

178		}

I now have a complete picture. Here is my report.

---

## Data Layer Location

The data/persistence layer lives in the **`/bench/repo/store/`** directory. This is a Go package (`package store`) that provides database access to all persistent entities. It follows a driver-based architecture supporting three database backends (SQLite, MySQL, PostgreSQL) with implementations in `/bench/repo/store/db/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/`.

Protobuf definitions for the store entities' payloads and settings are in `/bench/repo/proto/store/` (source `.proto` files) with generated Go code in `/bench/repo/proto/gen/store/`.

The canonical database schema is defined in the `LATEST.sql` migration files at `/bench/repo/store/migration/{sqlite,mysql,postgres}/LATEST.sql`.

---

## Complete List of Persistent Entity Types

There are **10 distinct persistent entity types** defined as database-backed tables. Each has a corresponding Go struct (and often Find/Update/Delete companion structs) in the store package:

| # | Entity Type | Go Struct | File | DB Table |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **User** | `User` | `/bench/repo/store/user.go` | `user` |
| 2 | **UserSetting** | `UserSetting` | `/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go` | `user_setting` |
| 3 | **UserIdentity** | `UserIdentity` | `/bench/repo/store/user_identity.go` | `user_identity` |
| 4 | **Memo** | `Memo` | `/bench/repo/store/memo.go` | `memo` |
| 5 | **MemoRelation** | `MemoRelation` | `/bench/repo/store/memo_relation.go` | `memo_relation` |
| 6 | **MemoShare** | `MemoShare` | `/bench/repo/store/memo_share.go` | `memo_share` |
| 7 | **Attachment** | `Attachment` | `/bench/repo/store/attachment.go` | `attachment` |
| 8 | **IdentityProvider** | `IdentityProvider` | `/bench/repo/store/idp.go` | `idp` |
| 9 | **Inbox** | `Inbox` | `/bench/repo/store/inbox.go` | `inbox` |
| 10 | **Reaction** | `Reaction` | `/bench/repo/store/reaction.go` | `reaction` |
| 11 | **InstanceSetting** | `InstanceSetting` | `/bench/repo/store/instance_setting.go` | `system_setting` |

### Additional Supporting Types (not separate tables, but important store-layer types)

- **`RowStatus`** (`/bench/repo/store/common.go`) -- shared enum (`NORMAL` / `ARCHIVED`) used by User and Memo.
- **`Role`** (`/bench/repo/store/user.go`) -- enum (`ADMIN` / `USER`) for user roles.
- **`Visibility`** (`/bench/repo/store/memo.go`) -- enum (`PUBLIC` / `PROTECTED` / `PRIVATE`) for memo visibility.
- **`InboxStatus`** (`/bench/repo/store/inbox.go`) -- enum (`UNREAD` / `ARCHIVED`) for inbox items.
- **`MemoRelationType`** (`/bench/repo/store/memo_relation.go`) -- enum (`REFERENCE` / `COMMENT`).
- **`DeleteUserResult`** (`/bench/repo/store/user_delete.go`) -- result struct returned when deleting a user.
- **`PATQueryResult`** / **`RefreshTokenQueryResult`** (`/bench/repo/store/user_setting.go`) -- query result structs for PAT and refresh token lookups.
- **`AuthenticationConfigState`** / **`AuthenticationConfigMutation`** (`/bench/repo/store/auth_config.go`) -- transactional types for atomic authentication configuration changes.
- **`deploymentConfiguration`** (`/bench/repo/store/store.go`) -- in-memory struct for file-backed identity providers and instance settings.

### Protobuf-Defined Payload/Setting Messages

The proto store layer (`/bench/repo/proto/store/`) defines structured payloads serialized as JSON columns within the tables above:

- `/bench/repo/proto/store/attachment.proto` -- `AttachmentPayload`, `AttachmentStorageType`
- `/bench/repo/proto/store/idp.proto` -- `IdentityProvider`, `IdentityProviderConfig`, `OAuth2Config`
- `/bench/repo/proto/store/inbox.proto` -- `InboxMessage`
- `/bench/repo/proto/store/instance_setting.proto` -- `InstanceSetting`, `InstanceBasicSetting`, `InstanceGeneralSetting`, `InstanceStorageSetting`, `InstanceMemoRelatedSetting`, `InstanceTagsSetting`, `InstanceNotificationSetting`, `InstanceAISetting`
- `/bench/repo/proto/store/memo.proto` -- `MemoPayload`
- `/bench/repo/proto/store/user_setting.proto` -- `UserSetting`, `GeneralUserSetting`, `ShortcutsUserSetting`, `TagsUserSetting`, `RefreshTokensUserSetting`, `PersonalAccessTokensUserSetting`, `WebhooksUserSetting`

### Driver Interface

The full `Driver` interface at `/bench/repo/store/driver.go` confirms the complete set of CRUD operations across all 11 entity types listed above (User, UserSetting, UserIdentity, Memo, MemoRelation, MemoShare, Attachment, IdentityProvider, Inbox, Reaction, InstanceSetting).
